correctness.rationale: For every positive height/side ratio the measure is explicitly specified. The proof computes the exact common offset interval for the two triangular and three rectangular faces, integrates its positive-part decomposition over vertical normal coordinate, then exactly integrates the three equilateral sine-gap expressions over azimuth. The independent crossed-edge expectation yields the remaining two probabilities. The derivative factorization gives a comparison of a strictly increasing function with a strictly decreasing one, proving a single inflection and hence a unique stationary maximum. Positive endpoint limits exclude hidden maxima. The actual embedded check_prism.py was run successfully and tested independent 2D face-interval quadratures and 3D edge-count samples. No finite test is used to justify the continuum theorem.

value.rationale: Right equilateral triangular prisms form the canonical smallest five-facet prism family. The complete exact probability law is a natural stereological invariant sensitive to height/side ratio, not a contrived finite search. The unique aspect ratio for pentagonal sections and limiting triangle/quadrilateral regimes are sharp structural geometric conclusions. They supply a useful benchmark for more general prismatoids and disambiguate invariant Crofton sampling from unweighted orientations. Correctness and reproducibility do not alone establish this value; the complete classification and unique nontrivial extremum do.
